openQuestions.question: How should an unqualified screen select among multiple configured teams?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Added optional team arguments; unscoped status discovers a single team and refuses ambiguity.

openQuestions.question: How should raw frontmatter render when the payload supplies only the parsed body?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Rendered the real body as Markdown and hid unavailable frontmatter.

openQuestions.question: How can one git child distinguish a missing skills tree from an invalid ref when git returns the same diagnostic?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Used a second read-only ref verification only on that ambiguous failure.

openQuestions.question: How should installed state be mapped before structured placement fields arrive?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Accepted only unambiguous placement-recorded sentences for the selected team; did not infer installation from disk presence.

openQuestions.question: What behavior should Recently updated eventually provide?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Carried dates without implementing sorting, as explicitly scoped.

openQuestions.question: What should the real install scope selector show without supported scope selection or project-folder data?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Kept sample scope choices in the mock; the real flow leaves the selector empty and delegates target selection to the CLI.

openQuestions.question: Should maintainer-owned adapter documentation now describe Library and Skill detail as served?
openQuestions.conservativeChoice: Left README.md, GAPS.md and FIDELITY.md unchanged and recorded the needed update.

deviations.what: The real SKILL.md tab does not display frontmatter.
deviations.why: The specified wire payload contains no raw frontmatter or license; synthesizing source content would violate data honesty.

deviations.what: Team discovery can issue status without --team.
deviations.why: The existing screen context supplies no selected team. All subsequent team-specific reads include --team.

deviations.what: The missing-tree diagnostic can require two git children for version lookup.
deviations.why: A second verification distinguishes a valid ref without skills from an invalid ref; normal lookup remains one child.
